meta_policy_notes: The hierarchical NEXUS agent for WalkerWalk employs a meta-policy to choose among specialized skills. Each skill is defined with permissive and overlapping activation rules, ensuring that the high-level controller always has multiple plausible options. Reward functions are designed to provide dense gradients, with a clear emphasis on the primary progress term for each skill, balanced by secondary stabilization terms and a consistent action penalty. This setup encourages the agent to learn robust and adaptable behaviors for standing and walking.

skills.name: get_up
skills.description: Focuses on getting the walker from a fallen or low-height state to a standing posture.

reward_terms.description: Strongly encourage reaching and maintaining the target torso height.
Penalize deviation from an upright torso posture.
Penalize high joint speeds to prevent flailing.

skills.name: walk_steady
skills.description: Aims to achieve and maintain a modest forward velocity while keeping a stable, upright posture. This is the primary goal-oriented skill.

reward_terms.description: Primary reward for moving forward at a positive velocity.
Encourage maintaining a good torso height while walking.
Penalize deviation from an upright torso posture to maintain balance.
Penalize high joint speeds to encourage smooth movement.

skills.name: maintain_posture
skills.description: Focuses purely on maintaining an upright and stable posture, especially when the walker is already standing or slightly off-balance, without a strong emphasis on forward motion.

reward_terms.description: Strong reward for maintaining the target torso height.
Strong penalty for any deviation from an upright torso posture.
Penalize high joint speeds to encourage stillness and stability.
